title: Would You Want CRM Stock Back At The Price It Just Left?
detail:
Would You Want CRM Stock Back At The Price It Just Left?
Trefis Team
Thu, September 17, 2026 at 12:06 PM MDT 4 min read
CRM
ORCL
NOW
MSFT
HUBS
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
Image from Pixabay

Salesforce (CRM) trades near $250 a share, close to its 52-week high after a fast three-month run. Selling a put pays you now for agreeing to buy it much lower later, and you keep the payment either way. The catch: you only want this if you would be glad to own Salesforce at that lower price. The open part of that answer is how much its new agent products can actually be charged for.

The Trade: Generating a 10% Yield with a 30% Cushion

Sell a put option on CRM expiring 9/17/2027, with a strike price of $175.

Collect roughly $1,060 in premium per contract (each contract covers 100 shares).

That works out to about 6.0% annualized on the $17,500 of cash you set aside to secure the trade.

Park that cash in Treasury bills or a Treasury money-market fund yielding roughly 4.1%, and your total yield climbs to about 10.1%.

And if CRM falls below $175, you buy it at $175, an effective entry near $164.40 a share after the premium, about a 34% discount to today's $250.10.

Two Ways This Plays Out, Both Pay You

If CRM stays above $175 through 9/17/2027, the put expires worthless and you simply keep the full $1,060 premium. That is about 6.0% annualized on the $17,500 you set aside over 366 days, while that same collateral keeps earning the ~4.1% T-bill yield on top, for the ~10.1% total above. You never buy the stock and keep the income, free to do it again.

If CRM closes below $175, you are assigned and buy 100 shares at $175. The $1,060 premium you already pocketed lowers your effective cost to about $164.40 a share, roughly a 34% discount to today's price, though if the stock has fallen further by then you would be holding a paper loss.

So the question that matters is what you would own if the shares land in your account.

How Far Would The CRM Stock Have To Fall?

Far, though the shares were well below today's level three months ago, and CRM traded as low as about $150 inside the past 52 weeks. It has gained more than 50% over the past three months. Stretch the window to twelve months and the gain is about 4%, against close to 16% for the S&P 500.

The entire twelve-month gain, and more, arrived in the last three months. The entire twelve-month gain, and more, arrived in the last three months. Assignment is not a bargain handed to you. It is a purchase, at a price the stock reaches only by falling.

Is Salesforce Still Growing Underneath The Agent Story?

Yes, and faster than it was. Revenue grew 11.2% over the past twelve months, against a 9.9% average over the past three years. Management says customer attrition ran near its lowest level ever in fiscal Q2 2027, which is a real answer to two quarters of predictions about the end of software.

JPMorgan highlighted premium upgrades and Agentforce customer data.

Stifel said Salesforce has "six distinct ways" to monetize AI across its products and services.

RBC Capital remained cautious, citing positive demand signals but mixed feedback on pricing.

Salesforce (CRM) stock fell in the morning trade on Thursday despite a wave of Wall Street price-target hikes following the company's Dreamforce investor day, with analysts citing Salesforce's growing AI business and the potential for a higher valuation.

Stifel, Canaccord Genuity and Guggenheim each raised their price targets to $300, while BMO Capital lifted its target to $285. JPMorgan called the event "incrementally positive for the re-rating thesis," citing premium upgrades and Agentforce customer data that it said could support higher spending by Salesforce's existing customers.

The analyst reaction comes with little change to Salesforce's financial outlook. Management reiterated its fiscal 2030 revenue target of $63 billion and kept its fiscal 2027 guidance unchanged.

CRM stock fell nearly 3% in midday trade, with retail sentiment trending in the 'bearish' zone on Stocktwits over the past day.

Several firms came away from Dreamforce more positive on Salesforce's ability to make money from AI.

Stifel said Salesforce has "six distinct ways" to monetize AI. These include selling more core licenses, premium upgrades, Agentforce, Data 360, Agent Fabric and APIs, MCPs and infrastructure.

Canaccord pointed to positive signs in Salesforce's pipeline, sales coverage and contract activity. Meanwhile, Guggenheim said it had a more open view of Salesforce's potential after the event, although it still sees some of the risks it had flagged before Dreamforce.

BMO also became more positive on Salesforce's ability to benefit from enterprise AI. The firm said new products and partnerships, including AIforce, could make it easier for customers to adopt the technology and create more value over time.

RBC Capital was more cautious. The firm said its checks with Salesforce partners showed improving demand but mixed feedback on pricing. It kept its 'Sector Perform' rating and $250 price target.

title: How Much Upside Is Left In Adobe Stock?
detail:
How Much Upside Is Left In Adobe Stock?
Trefis Team

ADBE
^GSPC
CRM
GOOG
ORCL
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
Image from Pixabay

Adobe (ADBE) trades near $250, down about 28% over the past year while the S&P 500 gained about 16%. Over the past three months the stock has returned about 21%. The market pays 13.9 times trailing earnings for a company that just reported record quarterly revenue. A multiple that low prices Adobe as if meaningful growth is off the table. The scenario below tests that pricing, and its answer rests on whether Adobe's free users ever start paying.

Where Would Adobe's Next Leg Come From?

Revenue does most of the work. The scenario grows it 10.3% a year for three years, a light haircut to the 11.5% Adobe managed over the past twelve months. Margin takes a little off, and earnings still rise about a third.

The lever sits in the creative franchise. Creative and marketing professionals brought in $4.65 billion of Adobe's $6.56 billion of subscription revenue in fiscal Q3 2026. Acrobat and Express sit behind them, with monthly active users past 900 million.

Then the multiple takes its turn. Adobe's P/E of 13.9x sits against a three-year average of 30.8x, and the scenario lets it re-rate part of the way, to 15.6x, because growth and margins are holding up. On those assumptions the stock would be worth about $374 in three years, roughly 49% above today.

What Has To Go Right For Adobe To Get There?

Adobe raised its revenue targets in September, but that guidance covers only the final quarter of fiscal 2026. Beyond that single quarter, virtually the entire three-year scenario is an extrapolation rather than management guidance.

Adobe's backlog of contracted revenue, which it calls RPO, grew 8% year over year in fiscal Q3 2026. Management ties that single-digit pace to its own choice: Adobe is routing new users into a free funnel instead of into paid contracts.

So Adobe is trading revenue today for users it hopes to charge later. Creative freemium monthly active users, which overlap with the Express footprint, crossed 100 million (up over 70% year over year) and sit in the free tier by design.

Management says that engagement is starting to translate into recurring revenue, and Firefly's ending recurring revenue across its apps and credit packs grew 40% quarter over quarter. Adobe also held off on Creative Cloud pricing actions, calling them short-term relief that would have mattered less than winning users.
